headline: Computational tools embed design and analysis safeguards into biology workflows
label: Computational Biology Workflow Tools
summary: Recent preprints and papers add pre-execution checks for primer design, differential expression assumptions, and proteomics run randomization.
synthesis: The common thread across these items is procedural safeguarding built directly into computational workflows, rather than a new algorithm. PEEK unifies silent-mutation discovery, restriction-site insertion, and primer design on a single Tm model, with Tm matched to the NEB Q5 calculator and validated by whole-plasmid sequencing. DE-Rigor-Agent screens six bulk RNA-seq differential expression methods for assumption compatibility before execution. WorkListGenerator structures proteomics project metadata and block-randomizes LC-MS run order, and BIOREDIS integrates nine biological resources for end-to-end design of RNA and DNA therapeutics. The items are heterogeneous in data type and pipeline stage, so the dominant thread is methodological infrastructure rather than a shared analytical advance. What is new is that each tool encodes a specific check, whether assumption screening, randomization, or Tm consistency, into the design or analysis step itself.
